messages:
maria: quick thread — security did a quick sweep and flagged deploy privileges as a low-medium risk. they want a clear checklist for who can deploy to prod and how temporary elevate access should work. can we map this out?

alex: yep. i'd like a minimal policy we can ship fast:
- require MFA for all human deployers
- short-lived elevation tokens for non-owners (30-60m)
- deploy approval for >minor changes (1 approval)
- emergency bypass for oncall with audit/logging

sanjay: oncall emergency bypass is critical. during incidents we can't wait for approval chain. propose:
- oncall role has scoped "incident-deploy" with MFA + auto-revoke after 120m
- every bypass auto-creates a ticket and pings incident channel

olivia: security notes:
- enforce per-user MFA (no shared accounts)
- rotate deployer service account keys quarterly
- require at least one of: github org membership + SSO group to be in deployer role
- logs must include who triggered elevation and the diff sha

rachel: deploy-bot pulled last 30 days of deployers and output (sanitized):
```
deploy-bot: recent_deployers: [alex, sanjay, rachel, mia, dmitri]
deploy-bot: service_accounts: [svc-deployer-1, svc-ci-runner]
```

maria: nice. let's sketch the config we want in platform config so devex/infra can implement quickly — example YAML idea:
```
roles:
  - name: deployer
    mfa_required: true
    elevation_max_minutes: 60
    approval_required_for: ["major", "migration"]
  - name: oncall-incident
    mfa_required: true
    elevation_max_minutes: 120
    bypass_audit: true
service_accounts:
  rotate_every_days: 90
```

alex: implementation notes:
- we can add a short-lived STS-style token flow tied to SSO group membership
- infra will auto-create audit event with PR link + git sha when someone uses elevation
- need a migration plan for existing deployer service accounts

olivia: also add enforcement window for change windows. if it's within change freeze, elevation should be blocked unless 2nd approval and sec signoff.

sanjay: ops question — how do we treat CI-driven deploys? some pipelines run as svc accounts and need longer TTLs. recommend: keep svc accounts but force token exchange so actions are attributable to pipeline run + commit metadata. rotate keys and put stricter network ACLs.

maria: action items:
- alex -> draft RBAC and elevation flow PR (owner) — target: EOD Thu
- sanjay -> define oncall incident bypass playbook + ticket automation
- olivia -> update security checklist and add change-freeze exception process
- rachel -> run one-off deployer audit and share gaps by tomorrow

alex: putting todos in a GH issue now and will link here :link: 

olivia: thumbs up. once PR is ready security will do quick review and we'll schedule a 20m sync with infra.

maria: thanks all. small, measurable changes only — we should avoid blocking day-to-day deploys. if anyone wants to push back on specifics, ping me or add to the GH issue. :thumbsup:
